concept.name: Hull moving average
concept.definition: Alan Hull's moving average (2005), engineered to nearly eliminate lag while retaining smoothness by combining weighted moving averages of different lengths with a lag-canceling correction term.
concept.intuition: An average designed to hug price closely without becoming jagged — fast like a short WMA, smooth like a long one.
concept.mechanics: Compute WMA(n/2) and WMA(n) of price, form the raw series 2*WMA(n/2) - WMA(n) to cancel lag, then smooth the result with a WMA of length sqrt(n), rounding non-integer periods to whole numbers.
concept.formula: HMA(n) = WMA( 2*WMA(P, n/2) - WMA(P, n), sqrt(n) ), where WMA(P, m) is the m-period weighted moving average of price.
concept.failure_modes: Reduced lag means reduced noise filtering: it whipsaws in sideways markets and remains a trend-follower, not a predictor.
concept.misconceptions: Hull himself advises against HMA crossover systems — crossovers exploit lag differences that the HMA was built to remove; use turns in the HMA's direction instead.
concept.example: For an 11-period HMA, use WMA(6) and WMA(11) for the raw line, then smooth with a 3-period WMA (sqrt(11) = 3.3 rounds to 3).
